## TL;DR

Updated `just release <version>` so the version bump and committed release record are prepared together before checks. The recipe calls a Bun script that uses the same entry builder and release-surface writer as the Releases page, then stages `package.json`, `release-history.json`, and `CHANGELOG.md` in one release commit. A guarded exit trap restores those files if the recipe fails after beginning the bump and before the changes are committed. The requested `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final tree.

## Work and rationale

The reported failure came from two release entry points treating the version differently. The Releases page writes both structured history and the changelog, while `just release` only changed the manifest. The history is consumed by `shared/release.ts` and other surfaces, so a version-only commit leaves the public release stamp behind and fails the committed-history assertion.

I added `createReleaseHistoryEntry` to `src/server/release-history.ts`. It accepts a version, commit subjects, and an optional date, and produces the standard version, `v` tag, UTC date, and rendered notes. The Releases page now uses this builder for its record entry while preserving supplied notes and known issues. The new `scripts/write-release-record.ts` also uses that builder and calls `writeReleaseSurfaces`, so the CLI recipe and Releases page share the format and write path rather than maintaining separate JSON and markdown logic.

The script validates the semantic version, collects up to 300 commit subjects since the most recent tag (or from the full history when no tag exists), and writes the record through the shared module. Its note order follows the Releases page’s `collectReleaseCommits` output. `just release` invokes the script immediately after bumping `package.json`; after checks pass, the recipe stages all three release files and commits them together. Tagging and pushing remain after the checks and commit, as before.

The recipe uses a Bash exit trap to recover from a failed bump or failed checks. A `bump_started` guard ensures the cleanup does not touch files when the recipe exits during preflight, such as when the tree is already dirty or the release tag exists. After mutation begins, a nonzero exit restores the three release files from `HEAD`. Once the release commit succeeds, restoring from `HEAD` leaves that committed release intact if a later tag or push operation fails.

The regression test in `release-history.test.ts` exercises the shared entry builder with a fixed UTC timestamp and commit list, verifies the record is written, and checks that the recipe invokes the writer and stages the record files. This ties the recipe’s record step to the code used by the Releases page without trying to run the release recipe itself, which would perform an actual release commit, tag, and push.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the recipe and the Releases page implementation. The release history writer already provided the necessary idempotent `writeReleaseSurfaces` operation, and the page already used `renderDefaultReleaseNotes` and `releaseDate`. Reusing these primitives through a shared entry builder was the smallest way to keep both entry points consistent. I considered constructing the JSON and changelog in the recipe, but that would duplicate the format and break the acceptance requirement that the release record use the same code as the page.

I also reviewed the rollback boundary. Restoring only `package.json` would still leave a release record that claims a version which did not pass checks. Restoring the manifest and both surfaces together covers the complete set of release files. The trap is enabled for the recipe but only acts after the version update begins, preserving the recipe’s existing refusal behavior for dirty trees and duplicate tags.

## Challenges and blockers

The first check run exposed a formatter issue in the new script. I ran `bun run fmt` as required and reran the exact changed-path check. One subsequent remote run failed in an unrelated reviewer-chat test because an asynchronous spawned-process assertion did not observe the expected mission text. That test passed when run alone; the following full scoped check passed. I left that unrelated test untouched because the failure did not reproduce in isolation and concerned no release code.

RepoOS’s remote validation initially skipped two hosts after network throughput probes timed out. It continued to Mini, where the final full changed-path tests, build, and browser gate completed successfully. The worktree’s local guards also passed. No release version was bumped and no release tag or push was created during this task.

## Key learnings

The release record is not a cosmetic changelog: it is the committed source of truth used by public version surfaces, so every release entry point must update it before the checks and commit. The shared release-history module is the correct boundary for the standard record builder and writer. A release recipe’s rollback should cover the manifest and every generated release surface, but it must be gated so early preflight failures cannot overwrite preexisting user changes.

The final check was `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. Its remote build and scoped test suite passed; the local format, lint, build, contrast audit, branch-artifact guard, and UI smoke checks passed. The suite reported 137 changed-path test files passing, with one test skipped.
